scenarios.name: Dry-run on a clean target
scenarios.given: An empty Git repository and a selected distribution version
scenarios.when: The operator runs the installer with --dry-run
scenarios.then: The command reports planned managed files and makes no mutation.

scenarios.name: Apply on a clean target
scenarios.given: A clean target and an approved manifest
scenarios.when: The operator runs the installer apply command
scenarios.then: Only manifest-owned files are created and a status command reports their version.

scenarios.name: Collision with target-owned file
scenarios.given: A target has a file at a managed destination that is not owned by the installer
scenarios.when: The operator runs apply without an explicit collision choice
scenarios.then: The command fails or skips according to the approved policy and leaves that file unchanged.

scenarios.name: Unsafe target rejection
scenarios.given: The selected path is not an existing Git worktree, is a subdirectory, or resolves through a symlink/reparse point
scenarios.when: The operator requests plan or apply
scenarios.then: The command rejects the target before mutation and reports the reason.

scenarios.name: Untrusted source and state rejection
scenarios.given: Source content or installer state contains unapproved agent instructions, scripts, secret-like paths, forged ownership, or altered provenance
scenarios.when: The operator requests install or update
scenarios.then: The command rejects the operation before mutation and records an actionable diagnostic.

scenarios.name: Interrupted multi-file apply
scenarios.given: A later file copy fails or the target changes during apply
scenarios.then: The staged operation rolls back atomically and leaves the target and ownership state unchanged.
